prompt.adult: Isaiah 60 opens as the city is in her light. According to 60:1, what does Isaiah speak first, before “For your light has come”?
prompt.child: Isaiah speaks to a city as the light God has given her arrives. What does he say first?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 60:1: what does he speak first, before “For your light has come”?
prompt.older: According to Isaiah 60:1, what does Isaiah say first?

verses.text: Arise, shine; For your light has come! And the glory of the LORD is risen upon you.

explanation.child: Look at the opening call of verse 1.
explanation.teen: 60:1 opens with a call, then a reason. Read the call.
explanation.older: They open 60:1, before “For your light has come.”

teaching.extended_explanation: 60:1 also says, “And the glory of the LORD is risen upon you.”

prompt.adult: Isaiah 56:3 speaks of the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD. In 56:5, what will the LORD give them in His house and within His walls, beyond that of sons and daughters?
prompt.child: God makes a promise to people who might have felt left out. What does He say He will give them in His house, beyond that of sons and daughters?
prompt.older: Read with 56:3, what does 56:5 say the LORD will give them in His house?

verses.text: Do not let the son of the foreigner Who has joined himself to the LORD Speak, saying, “The LORD has utterly separated me from His people”; Nor let the eunuch say, “Here I am, a dry tree.”
Even to them I will give in My house And within My walls a place and a name Better than that of sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name That shall not be cut off.

explanation.child: Look right after “within My walls” in verse 5.
explanation.teen: 56:3 speaks of the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD; 56:5 states the gift in His house. Read that gift.

teaching.extended_explanation: 56:5 also says that gift shall not be cut off. 56:3 warns the foreigner not to say he is utterly separated.
teaching.takeaway: The LORD will give them a place and a name.

prompt.adult: Isaiah 58:9 says, “You shall cry, and He will say, ‘Here I am.’ ” In 58:6, after “To loose the bonds of wickedness,” what does the LORD list as part of the fast He has chosen?
prompt.child: The LORD describes the kind of fast He has chosen. After loosing the bonds of wickedness, what does He say to undo?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 58:6: “To undo” what, “To let the oppressed go free”?
prompt.older: Read with 58:9, what does 58:6 say to undo?

verses.text: “Is this not the fast that I have chosen: To loose the bonds of wickedness, To undo the heavy burdens, To let the oppressed go free, And that you break every yoke?
Then you shall call, and the LORD will answer; You shall cry, and He will say, ‘Here I am.’ “If you take away the yoke from your midst, The pointing of the finger, and speaking wickedness,

explanation.child: Look right after “To undo” in verse 6.
explanation.teen: 58:9 promises an answer; 58:6 lists the chosen fast. Read the second item.

teaching.extended_explanation: 58:6 also says, “To let the oppressed go free, And that you break every yoke.” 58:9 says, “You shall cry, and He will say, ‘Here I am.’ ”
teaching.takeaway: The chosen fast is to undo the heavy burdens.

prompt.adult: Isaiah 65:1 says, “Here I am, here I am,” to a nation that had not sought Him. In 65:5, what do those people say after “Keep to yourself, Do not come near me, For”?
prompt.child: Isaiah describes people who want others to stay away from them. What do they say after “Do not come near me, For”?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 65:5: “Do not come near me, For” what?
prompt.older: Read with 65:1, what does 65:5 say after “For”?

verses.text: “I was sought by those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me. I said, ‘Here I am, here I am,’ To a nation that was not called by My name.
Who say, ‘Keep to yourself, Do not come near me, For I am holier than you!’ These are smoke in My nostrils, A fire that burns all the day.

explanation.child: Look right after “For” in the quotation in verse 5.
explanation.teen: 65:1 is the LORD’s call; 65:5 quotes what these people say. Read the last claim.

teaching.extended_explanation: 65:5 also says, “These are smoke in My nostrils.” 65:1 says He was found by those who did not seek Him.
teaching.takeaway: They say, “I am holier than you!”

prompt.adult: Isaiah 65:14 says My servants shall sing for joy of heart. In 66:1, what does the LORD say first, before He speaks of the earth?
prompt.child: The LORD speaks of where He sits. What does He say first in 66:1?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 66:1: “Thus says the LORD:” what first?
prompt.older: Read with 65:14, what does 66:1 say first?

verses.text: Behold, My servants shall sing for joy of heart, But you shall cry for sorrow of heart, And wail for grief of spirit.
Thus says the LORD: “Heaven is My throne, And earth is My footstool. Where is the house that you will build Me? And where is the place of My rest?

explanation.adult: Read the start of the LORD’s words in 66:1.
explanation.child: Look at the first claim in verse 1.
explanation.teen: 65:14 contrasts song and sorrow; 66:1 opens with where He sits. Read that opening claim.
explanation.older: It is the first claim of 66:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 66:1 also asks, “Where is the house that you will build Me?” 65:14 says the others shall cry for sorrow of heart.
teaching.takeaway: The LORD says, “Heaven is My throne.”

prompt.adult: Isaiah 56:1 says, “Keep justice, and do righteousness.” In 58:10, after “Then your light shall dawn in the darkness,” how does the verse end?
prompt.child: Isaiah describes kindness to the hungry. How does 58:10 end?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 58:10: “And your darkness shall be as” what?

choices.text: your darkness shall be as the moonlight
your darkness shall be as the noonday
your darkness shall be as the starlight
your darkness shall be as the sunrise

verses.text: Thus says the LORD: “Keep justice, and do righteousness, For My salvation is about to come, And My righteousness to be revealed.
If you extend your soul to the hungry And satisfy the afflicted soul, Then your light shall dawn in the darkness, And your darkness shall be as the noonday.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 10.
explanation.teen: 56:1 calls them to keep justice; 58:10 ends with this promise. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “And your darkness shall be as” in 58:10.

teaching.extended_explanation: 58:10 also says, “If you extend your soul to the hungry.” 56:1 says, “For My salvation is about to come.”
teaching.takeaway: Your darkness shall be as the noonday.

prompt.adult: Isaiah 56:4 speaks of the eunuchs who keep His Sabbaths. In 60:18, after violence is no longer heard in the land, what shall they call their walls?

prompt.teen: Isaiah 60:18: “But you shall call your walls” what?
prompt.older: Read with 56:4, what does 60:18 say they shall call their walls?

choices.text: you shall call your walls Strength
you shall call your walls Great Honor
you shall call your walls Salvation
you shall call your walls High Praise

verses.text: For thus says the LORD: “To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, And choose what pleases Me, And hold fast My covenant,
Violence shall no longer be heard in your land, Neither wasting nor destruction within your borders; But you shall call your walls Salvation, And your gates Praise.

explanation.child: Look right after “call your walls” in verse 18.
explanation.teen: 56:4 names those who keep His Sabbaths; 60:18 names what the walls shall be called. Read that name.

teaching.extended_explanation: 60:18 also says, “And your gates Praise.” 56:4 says they hold fast His covenant.
teaching.takeaway: They shall call their walls Salvation.

verses.text: Therefore your gates shall be open continually; They shall not be shut day or night, That men may bring to you the wealth of the Gentiles, And their kings in procession.
